name: local-missed-requirement
about: A local job whose earlier leads often missed a hard requirement or gave a wrong number.

area.label: Fixture Yard, IL
area.reason: Fixture: drivers within a day's drive of the yard.

history.text: Boostpoint 2026 benchmark, CDL drivers on Meta: an ad costing more than $42.00 per lead after 5 leads, or $85.00 spent with no lead, is where pausing is suggested.
Of 58 of our ad leads in the last 28 days, 44 were called and 25 were reached.
21 of 58 of our ad leads in the last 28 days did not meet a hard requirement of the opening.
9 of the 44 ad leads we called in the last 28 days had a wrong number.

output.audience: Experienced Class A drivers who want hourly pay, weekday work and to be home daily, and who accept touch freight in a day cab. Many earlier leads missed a hard requirement, so the ads should state the experience needed and the physical work plainly.

angles.idea: Say plainly who this job is for: Class A, the stated experience, and touch freight in a day cab.
angles.proof: The opening states its experience requirement and that the work is touch freight.
angles.why: Many earlier leads did not meet a hard requirement, so stating it up front is worth more than attracting more. Nothing has been measured about hooks or formats.

angles.idea: Lead with the hourly rate for local Class A delivery, and name health insurance beside it.
angles.proof: The opening pays the stated hourly rate and offers health insurance.
angles.why: Hourly pay is the plainest fact a local driver compares. This carrier has no ad results on the sheet, so nothing has been measured for this hook or format.

angles.idea: Lead with being home daily on a Monday to Friday schedule, shown as a quiet home street.
angles.proof: The opening offers home daily and runs Monday to Friday.
angles.why: The schedule is what sets local delivery apart from road work. No earlier ad results exist to weigh it against, and nothing has been measured about the format.

angles.idea: Lead with the day cab parked and ready, as the sign of local work with touch freight.
angles.proof: The job is driven in a day cab and involves touch freight.
angles.why: The equipment tells a driver at a glance what kind of work this is, and naming touch freight keeps it honest. Nothing has been measured about this hook or the still format.
